To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the X-ray spectrum of XTE J 1550-564 varies during individual X-ray shots and that this variability is different from that of Cyg X- 1, the only other microquasar for which shot-to-shot X-ray spectral variations have been studied.
the 13-60/2-13 kev hardness ratios during a XTE J155O-564 shot is lower than that of Cyg X- 1, and the 16-60/13-16 kev hardness ratios of XTE Jl550-564 is higher than that of Cyx X-1.

the X-ray spectral behavior during the shot in XTE J155O-564 is quite different from that in Cyg X-l, and that the physical processes that govern the X-ray emission in XTE Jl5lO-564 may be different than in Cyg X-I.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the X-ray variability of XTE J1650 - 564 during its initial rise.
the X-ray variability of microquasar Xte J1550 -564.
X-ray variability in XTE J155O-564.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the X-ray variability in XTE J155 0-564 and in Cyg X-l are different.
the microquasars XTE J155O-564 and Cyg X-3 are different from the black hole candidate Cyg X-l and from the low-mass X-ray binary Sco X-l, respectively.
the X-ray spectral properties in the initial rise of XTE J 1550-564 are different from those in the low state in Cyg X-l.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microquasar is in a different state than Cyg X- 1 and the physical processes at play in the low state are not the same as those in Cyg X-1.
the spectral behavior of XTE J 1550 - 584 is different from that of Cyg X- 1.
the spectral variability of the micro-quasar XTE J 1550 - 56 during the initial rise is different from that of Cyg X- 1, and is more similar to that of GX 339-4.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the X-ray variability of black hole binaries can be very complicated and that we need to be very careful when using time-domain techniques to study the variability.
the spectral behavior during a shot is not the same as that during steady emission, and that the spectral variability of a shot is different from that of a microquasar in the low state.
the X-ray spectra of the initial rise phase of XTE J 1550 - 584 are significantly different from that of the steady low state.
